class.name: NetwParticipant
class.brief_description: Live handle for one accepted session player.
class.description: One accepted membership, and the object is the membership. The session mints exactly one participant per acceptance and answers that same object every time, so [code]==[/code] returns "the same player" and a [Dictionary] keys on it directly. A membership is not a transport peer. [member peer_id] is where this player is reachable right now and is reused by whoever connects next, so a participant whose membership ended reports [member is_active] false and keeps the [member username] it joined under rather than reading whatever peer now holds that id. A membership is not a body either. [member players] is the set of bodies the session currently holds for it, which is empty for a spectator and holds more than one for a player the game gave several. [codeblock] var participant := api.peer_get_participant(peer_id) if participant.identity: greet(participant.username) for body: NetwEntity in participant.players: follow(body.owner) [/codeblock] Created by the session at the moment it accepts a join. A peer that has connected and not joined has no membership, so [method NetwMultiplayer.peer_get_participant] answers [code]null[/code] for it.

members.member: The validated auth identity for this peer, or [code]null[/code]. Present only when the session has an auth provider, and never replicated to other peers. Read from the session's own book through [method NetwMultiplayer.peer_get_identity], which is the one result to who authenticated.

Whether this membership is still the one the session holds. A handle a game kept across a disconnect answers [code]false[/code] here even when another player has since connected onto the same [member peer_id], which is what a game checks before acting on a participant it stored.
The transport peer this membership is currently reachable on. A routing detail rather than identity, because a reconnect reuses the id.

Every body the session currently holds for this membership, in no promised order. Answered live from the session rather than stored, so a body that despawned is gone from the next read. A participant nothing has spawned for answers an empty array, which is the honest reading for a spectator and for a player whose join handler has not placed it yet. Several bodies at once is ordinary, so a game that means one body reads the array and says which one it means.

The username this membership was accepted under, and the conventional save key when [member identity] is absent. Stamped at acceptance and never re-read, so it survives the membership ending and never reports a later player's name.
